groups.title: Laravel Queues
groups.question: Emails seem to send instantly in production, but requests have become slow, and a job that keeps failing is retried forever. Explain how Laravel queues should be set up.

followUps.Queue Drivers and the Sync Driver Trap: Why is the sync queue driver a trap in production?
followUps.Job Retries, Failures, and the Dead Lett: How should retries and failures be configured?

evidence.text: Laravel supports queue backends like Redis, SQS and the database.
The sync driver runs jobs immediately in the same request.
In production that makes requests wait for every job, defeating the purpose of queues.
Jobs set a maximum number of attempts.
Backoff adds increasing waits between attempts.
Jobs that still fail go to the failed jobs table for inspection and retry.

groups.title: Redis Integration
groups.question: Clearing the cache in production also wiped out all pending jobs, and you cannot see why the queue is backing up. Explain how you would configure Redis and monitor queues.

followUps.Redis for Caching vs Queuing — Separate: Why did clearing the cache destroy queued jobs?

evidence.text: Cache and queue both used the same Redis database by default.
Flushing the cache cleared everything in that database, including jobs.
Using separate Redis databases or connections keeps them apart.
Horizon is a dashboard for Redis queues.
It manages worker counts per queue from configuration.
It shows throughput, wait times and failed jobs, and can alert.

groups.title: Laravel Mail
groups.question: You need an order confirmation email that looks good, is easy to preview, and does not slow down checkout. Explain how Laravel Mail handles this.

followUps.Mailable Classes and Markdown Templates: What does a Mailable class contain?
followUps.Queueing Emails and Mail Drivers: How does queueing emails speed up checkout?

evidence.text: A Mailable holds the subject, recipients and template data.
Markdown templates give consistent, responsive email layouts.
Mailables can be previewed in the browser and tested.
Implementing ShouldQueue sends the email from a queue worker.
The request does not wait for the mail server.
Mail drivers like SMTP or an API service are configured separately.

groups.title: Laravel Notifications
groups.question: When an order ships, the customer should get an email, an in-app notification with an unread badge and maybe a text. Explain how Laravel notifications handle this.

followUps.Multi-Channel Notifications: How does one notification class send through several channels?
followUps.Database Notifications and Read State: How do database notifications support an unread count?

evidence.text: The via method lists channels like mail, database or SMS.
The class has a method for each channel's message.
All channels for that event live in one class.
Database notifications are stored in a notifications table.
A read_at timestamp marks whether each one was read.
Counting rows without read_at gives the unread badge.
